'''Dorothy Margaret Doig Edgington'''<ref>[https://www.bbk.ac.uk/about-us/fellows/dorothy-edginton Dorothy Edgington personal webpage, Birkbeck]</ref> [[Fellow of the British Academy|FBA]] (née '''Milne''', born 29 April 1941) is a British philosopher active in [[metaphysics]] and [[philosophical logic]].<ref>EDGINGTON, Prof. Dorothy Margaret Doig', Who's Who 2017, A & C Black, 2017; online edn, Oxford University Press, Nov 2016; online edn, Nov 2016  [http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U14635, accessed 9 Aug 2017]</ref>  She is particularly known for her work on the logic of [[conditional sentences|conditionals]] and [[vagueness]].<ref name=audit/>

==Life and education==
Dorothy Edgington was born on 29 April 1941 to Edward Milne and his wife Rhoda née Blair. She attended St Leonards School before going to [[St Hilda's College, Oxford]] to read PPE. She obtained her BA in 1964, followed in 1967 by a BPhil at [[Nuffield College, Oxford]].<ref>EDGINGTON, Prof. Dorothy Margaret Doig', Who's Who 2017, A & C Black, 2017; online edn, Oxford University Press, Nov 2016; online edn, Nov 2016  [http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U14635, accessed 9 Aug 2017]</ref>

==Career==
Most of Edgington's career was spent at [[Birkbeck College]]. In 1968, her first academic post was as a Lecturer in Philosophy at Birkbeck, remaining there until 1996. From 1996 until 2001, she was appointed Fellow of [[University College, Oxford]]. This was followed by a professorship at Birkbeck from 2001 to 2003. She was then [[Waynflete Professor of Metaphysical Philosophy]] at the [[University of Oxford]]<ref name=audit>{{cite news|title= Department audit |author= Sue James |url= http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/story.asp?storyCode=192253&sectioncode=26 |newspaper= The Times |date= 5 November 2004 |accessdate=25 December 2010}}</ref> from 2003<ref name=birkbeck>{{cite web|url=http://www.bbk.ac.uk/phil/news/dorothyedgington2|title=Prof. Dorothy Edgington returns to Birkbeck|accessdate=25 December 2010|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615071450/http://www.bbk.ac.uk/phil/news/dorothyedgington2/|archivedate=15 June 2011}}</ref> until  2006. Currently, she is a [[Emeritus|professor emeritus]] and a Fellow of [[Magdalen College, Oxford]] who teaches at Birkbeck again<ref name=birkbeck/> part-time. 

[[Birkbeck, University of London|Birkbeck College]] hosts a lecture series named after Edgington. The lectures were given by [[John McDowell]] in 2012, given by [[Rae Helen Langton|Rae Langton]] in 2014, and the Edgington Lectures were given by [[Kit Fine]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Edgington Lectures|url=http://edgingtonlectures.org|website=The Edgington Lectures|accessdate=16 August 2017}}</ref>

From 2004 to 2005, she was President of the [[Mind Association]]. Later, she became President of the [[Aristotelian Society]] from 2007 to 2008. She is a Fellow of the [[British Academy]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Dorothy Edgington|url=http://www.britac.ac.uk/user/2129|website=British Academy|accessdate=16 August 2017}}</ref>

In 2023, she was elected a member of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dorothy Edgington|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Edgington_Dorothy|work=Member|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2024-12-24}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
* 'The Paradox of Knowability' (1985), ''Mind'' 94:557–568.  Presents a resolution of [[Fitch's paradox]] based on [[situation semantics]].
* 'On Conditionals' (1995), ''Mind'' 104:235–329. Defends an epistemic theory of conditionals against a truth-functional one, as part of the Mind's state of the art series.
* 'Vagueness by Degrees'. In Rosanna Keefe & Peter Smith (eds.), ''Vagueness: A Reader''. MIT Press (1997)
* 'Counterfactuals and the Benefit of Hindsight'. In Phil Dowe & Paul Noordhof (eds.), ''Cause and Chance: Causation in an Indeterministic World''. Routledge (2004) 
* ''[http://plato.stanford.edu/entries/conditionals/ Conditionals]'' (2006), ''The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy''.
